tools.name: verify_provider
tools.description: PAID tool ($0.001 USDC via x402, Base). Verify a provider or source before an AI agent trusts or uses it. Returns live evidence only; unknown stays unknown. Send the x402 PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header on the /mcp request; without payment the call returns the canonical x402 challenge (HTTP 402, amount 100

tools.name: compare_providers
tools.description: Compare 2-5 providers side by side using live evidence gathered the same way verify_provider gathers it — identity, payment-readiness, and status evidence for each target, returned as a separate envelope per provider. No composite score is computed and no winner is declared; unknown evidence stays u

tools.name: check_identity
tools.description: Check live provider identity evidence: the published ERC-8004 agent identity document and its source/status envelope, returned exactly as observed. A successful fetch shows declared identity only — it is not external certification and not settlement verification — and missing evidence stays unknown

tools.name: check_payment
tools.description: Check live x402 payment readiness and real settlement evidence: the canonical x402 payment contract, the readiness endpoint, and recorded settlement evidence, returned as separate envelopes. A 402 challenge, a signature, a readiness flag, or an HTTP 200 alone does not prove settled, accepted deliver

tools.name: check_history
tools.description: Check recent evidence-backed provider history. Traffic volume is context only and is never presented as buyers, trust, or reputation.

tools.name: check_status
tools.description: Check whether the Provider Trust backend is live: returns the authoritative backend status envelope for the service that powers verify_provider, compare_providers, and the other checks. Use it to distinguish a Provider Trust outage from a target-side evidence gap before relying on any check result.

tools.name: canon_registry_bulk_lookup
tools.description: PAID tool ($0.01 USDC via x402, Base). Resolve up to 100 artifact freshness records in one call against live registries and cryptographically verified CANON publisher manifests: detects stale mirrors, superseded artifacts, and publisher/registry conflicts.
